correctness.rationale: Direct proof: rank-three and rank-four line-cover formulas distinguish orders two and three. For arbitrary affine planes of order at least four, Duplicator preserves an enhanced record on up to three selected objects (incidence, line parallelism, point collinearity, triple-line concurrency) and on the fourth selection matches all atomic incidence, sort and equality statements. Explicit witness inequalities include at least \(q^2-3q>0\) points off three lines, \(q-2>0\) points on one selected line off two others, and \((q-3)(q+1)>0\) lines through none of three points. Both independent exact finite-type implementations agree for fields of orders two, three and four; C++ additionally checks five and seven. No finite computation is used in place of infinite proof.

value.rationale: Finite affine planes form a classical natural family, with genuinely different orders and non-Desarguesian examples. Determining precisely what four rounds of sparse incidence-only FO logic can see is a motivated structural invariant, and the exact two exceptions and 36-element representative bound are both sharp. The back-and-forth proof depends on hidden parallelism, concurrency and line-avoidance margins, not merely on formula renaming or a routine field-size count.
